# Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic & Hijama Center (Karachi Hijama) - full text

> Sunnah hijama (wet and dry cupping therapy), Unani (Tibb) herbal medicine, homoeopathy and Reiki at a clinic in Model Colony, Karachi, Pakistan, plus hijama home service across Karachi and online consultations for patients abroad. Booking is by WhatsApp or phone.

## Key facts

- Name: Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic & Hijama Center
- Address: 20/32-33 Sardar Muhammad Ali Road, Nishterabad, Model Colony, Karachi 75100, Sindh, Pakistan (map: https://maps.app.goo.gl/VTyGuWixhJyLerCS6; coordinates 24.9072588, 67.1925137)
- Phone / WhatsApp: +92 322 2905560 (also +92 311 3023173 and +92 333 2259835)
- Hours: open daily, 3:00 PM to 10:00 PM
- Practitioner: Dr Misbah Shaheen Cheena (Hakeem), lead physician. The site states Dr Misbah is registered with the National Council for Homeopathy, the National Council for Tibb (Unani) and the Sindh Healthcare Commission, with certificates on display at the clinic. A qualified female practitioner is available for women patients on request.
- Serving Karachi since 1987 (the clinic's Google Business Profile also says "Established in 1987").
- Languages: English and Urdu
- Hygiene: new single-use cups and blades for every session.
- How to book: WhatsApp or call +92 322 2905560, or the booking form on the homepage (it opens a pre-filled WhatsApp message).

## Safety (who should not have wet cupping)

Wet cupping is not done during pregnancy. People on blood thinners or with a bleeding disorder, severe anaemia, an active infection or an acutely inflamed joint are advised against it or referred to a doctor first. Patients are asked about medicines and conditions before any session. Hijama, Unani, homoeopathy and Reiki are offered as traditional, complementary care; they are not a substitute for diagnosis or treatment by a doctor, and evidence for many uses is limited.

## Questions and answers from the site

Each answer is copied from the FAQ on the page named.

### Hijama in Karachi — Clinic & Home Service | Shaheen Shafi
Source: https://karachihijama.com/

Q: What is Hijama (cupping therapy)?
A: Hijama is a traditional cupping therapy practised in the Sunnah and in classical Unani (Tibb) medicine. Cups are applied to specific points on the body; in wet cupping a few tiny superficial scratches allow a small amount of blood to be drawn into the cup. We offer it as trusted, traditional Sunnah care.

Q: Which days are best for Hijama?
A: The Sunnah recommends the 17th, 19th and 21st of the Islamic (lunar) month, and especially Monday or Thursday. See the "Sunnah days" section above for today's Islamic date and the next recommended dates. These are traditional recommendations — Hijama can be done on other days too.

Q: Do you use single-use cups and blades?
A: Yes. We use single-use, disposable cups and blades and follow strict hygiene for every session — never reused. Sterile, single-use equipment is a core part of safe Hijama practice.

Q: Do you treat women?
A: Yes. We treat women and provide a respectful, private and calm setting for every patient. You are welcome to bring a female family member with you, and if you have any specific arrangements you'd like, please mention it on WhatsApp when booking.

Q: What are your timings?
A: We are open every day, 3:00 PM to 10:00 PM. WhatsApp is the fastest way to book — we usually reply within clinic hours.

Q: Where are you located?
A: Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic & Hijama Center is at 20/32-33 Sardar Muhammad Ali Road, Nishterabad, Model Colony, Karachi 75100, Pakistan. See the Location section for a map and directions.

Q: Is cupping therapy safe?
A: When done hygienically by a trained practitioner with single-use, sterile equipment, hijama is generally well tolerated; bruise-like marks and brief tiredness are common. Wet cupping is not done during pregnancy, and people on blood thinners or with a bleeding disorder are usually advised against it or asked to check with their doctor first. Tell us about your medicines and health when you book.

Q: How much does hijama cost in Karachi?
A: Our fixed prices: dry cupping Rs 1,800, single wet hijama Rs 2,500, full-body Sunnah hijama (~15 cups) Rs 4,200, and full-body hijama at your home anywhere in Karachi Rs 6,500. The full list is on our packages page.

Q: Do you offer hijama at home?
A: Yes. Home service is available across Karachi — including Gulshan-e-Iqbal, DHA, Clifton, Korangi, Saddar, Malir, PECHS, Bahadurabad, North Nazimabad, Federal B Area and Gulistan-e-Johar — at a fixed Rs 6,500 for a full-body session, with sterile single-use equipment. Book on WhatsApp.

Q: How do I book an appointment?
A: The easiest way is WhatsApp or a call on +92 322 2905560 during clinic hours (3:00 PM to 10:00 PM daily). You can also use the booking form on this page, which opens a pre-filled WhatsApp message.

Q: What is Unani medicine?
A: Unani (Tibb) is a classical system of traditional herbal medicine. A hakeem assesses your temperament and symptoms and suggests herbal preparations, diet and lifestyle guidance. It is offered as complementary care alongside, not instead of, your doctor's treatment.


### Hijama Prices in Karachi — Packages from Rs 1,800

Q: What is a Hijama course in Karachi?
A: At our clinic, a 'hijama course' means a structured treatment plan of multiple sessions rather than training to become a practitioner - for example, our Full Detox Course (12 sessions, PKR 28,000) is designed for a more thorough, ongoing wellness plan. If your concern needs more than one visit, we will recommend the right course length and space your sessions safely apart. We currently focus on patient care, not practitioner certification training.

Q: How many sessions are in a typical Hijama course?
A: It depends on your concern and the package you choose. Our Full Detox Course runs for 12 sessions, while for a specific issue we often suggest a shorter course of a few sessions spaced a few weeks apart, followed by occasional maintenance visits. Tell us your concern on WhatsApp and we will recommend the right length for you.

Q: Can I book a single Hijama session instead of a course?
A: Yes. A single Sunnah wet-cupping session is available and is a popular choice for general wellness or a one-off concern. If we feel a course would genuinely help you more, we will tell you honestly - but a single session is never a problem to book.


### Cupping Therapy in Karachi | Shaheen Shafi Hijama Center
Source: https://karachihijama.com/cupping-therapy-karachi.html

Q: What is the difference between wet cupping and dry cupping?
A: Dry cupping uses suction alone. Cups are placed on the skin, air is drawn out, and nothing else is done to the skin. Wet cupping, the classical hijama, adds a few tiny superficial scratches so that a small amount of blood is drawn into the cup. Wet cupping is what most people in Karachi mean when they say hijama. Dry cupping is gentler and is often chosen by people who are nervous about the scratches or who mainly want help with muscular tightness.

Q: Is cupping therapy painful?
A: Most patients describe the suction as a strong pulling or tightness rather than pain. In wet cupping the small scratches feel like a brief scratch or sting and are made only in the top layer of skin. If anything feels too strong at any point, tell Dr Misbah and the suction can be reduced immediately. Many people find the session itself relaxing and feel sleepy afterwards.

Q: How much does cupping therapy cost in Karachi?
A: The cost depends on whether you are having wet or dry cupping, how many points are treated, and whether you want the session at the clinic or at your home. Current session options are listed on our packages page, and you are welcome to message us on WhatsApp for a clear figure before you book. We will always tell you the price before your session starts, never after.

Q: Is a female practitioner available for women patients?
A: Yes. A qualified female practitioner is available at the clinic, so women patients can be treated comfortably and privately. Please mention it when you book on WhatsApp so we can arrange the right time slot for you. You are also welcome to bring a family member with you.

Q: Do you offer cupping therapy at home in Karachi?
A: Yes. Home service is available across much of Karachi, including Model Colony, Gulshan-e-Iqbal, DHA, Malir, North Nazimabad, Bahadurabad, Clifton, Federal B Area, Gulistan-e-Johar, Korangi, PECHS and Saddar. The same sterile single-use equipment is used at home as at the clinic. Send us your area on WhatsApp and we will confirm availability and timing.

Q: How long do cupping marks last?
A: Round marks where the cups were placed are normal and expected. They are caused by the suction, not by injury, and are usually painless. They typically fade over several days, and are generally lighter after dry cupping than after wet cupping. If you have an event coming up, tell us and we can plan the placement or the timing around it.

Q: Can I have cupping therapy if I am pregnant, taking blood thinners, or have a bleeding disorder?
A: Please tell us before you book. Pregnancy, blood thinning medication such as warfarin, and any bleeding or clotting disorder all need care, and wet cupping may not be appropriate. The same applies if you have anaemia, uncontrolled diabetes, an active skin infection at the site, or if you feel very weak or dehydrated. For any diagnosed medical condition, check with your doctor first. We would rather turn a session down than take a risk with your health.

Q: Where is the clinic and what are your timings?
A: Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic and Hijama Center is at 20/32-33 Sardar Muhammad Ali Road, Nishterabad, Model Colony, Karachi 75100. We are open daily from 3:00 PM to 10:00 PM. You can reach us on WhatsApp or phone at +92 322 2905560, +92 311 3023173 or +92 333 2259835. Booking ahead is best, especially in the evening.


### Hijama Center for Ladies Near Me in Karachi | Shaheen Shafi
Source: https://karachihijama.com/hijama-for-ladies-karachi.html

Q: Is there a female hijama practitioner at your Karachi center?
A: Yes. A qualified female practitioner is available for women patients. Because she is not on duty every single hour, please say clearly on WhatsApp when you book that you want a lady practitioner, and we will give you the times she can see you. If we cannot arrange it for the slot you asked for, we will tell you honestly rather than let you arrive and be disappointed.

Q: How is my privacy protected during the session?
A: Only the small area being cupped is uncovered at any one time, and the rest of you stays covered throughout. You keep your dupatta or scarf on. You are welcome to bring your mother, sister, husband or a friend into the room with you. If you would like any particular arrangement for privacy, ask when you book and we will tell you plainly what we can and cannot do that day.

Q: What should I wear to a ladies hijama appointment?
A: Wear a loose shalwar kameez in a dark or old colour, ideally one that opens at the back or has a wide neckline, so the upper back and shoulders can be reached without you undressing. Avoid tight sleeves and delicate fabric. Bring your usual scarf or dupatta. A few small marks of oil or blood can happen, so please do not wear something you would be upset to stain.

Q: Can I have hijama during my period?
A: Most women prefer to wait until their period has finished, and we generally suggest the same, mainly for comfort and because you may already be feeling low on energy. It is a matter of timing and how you feel, not a medical prohibition we can rule on. If your bleeding is heavy or prolonged, or you have been told you are anaemic, please speak to your doctor first and mention it to us when you book.

Q: Is hijama safe during pregnancy or while breastfeeding?
A: If you are pregnant, or think you may be, tell us before you book. We do not perform wet cupping during pregnancy. If you are breastfeeding, tell us as well so the session can be kept light and short and you can be advised on eating and drinking properly afterwards. In both cases we would rather you check with your own doctor first, and we will not press you to book.

Q: Can hijama treat PCOS or help with fertility?
A: We will not claim that. Hijama is a traditional Sunnah and Unani practice offered as complementary care, and it is not a treatment or a cure for PCOS, infertility, or any other diagnosed condition. Some women come to us for general wellbeing alongside the care their own doctor is giving them, and that is how we would ask you to think about it. Please continue your medical treatment and follow your doctor's advice.

Q: Do you do hijama for ladies at home in Karachi?
A: Yes. Home service is available across Karachi, including Model Colony, Gulshan-e-Iqbal, DHA, Malir, North Nazimabad, Bahadurabad, Clifton, Federal B Area, Gulistan-e-Johar, Korangi, PECHS and Saddar. The same sterile single-use cups and blades are brought to you. Many women choose home service simply because it is the most private option, and because a female family member can be in the room. If you want a lady practitioner for a home visit, please request it at the time of booking.

Q: What does hijama for ladies cost, and what are your timings?
A: Session options are listed on our packages page, and we will confirm the exact figure on WhatsApp before you come so there is no awkwardness about money on the day. The clinic is open from 3:00 PM to 10:00 PM daily at 20/32-33 Sardar Muhammad Ali Road, Nishterabad, Model Colony, Karachi. You can message or call +92 322 2905560, +92 311 3023173 or +92 333 2259835.


### Wet Cupping (Sunnah Hijama) in Karachi | Shaheen Shafi
Source: https://karachihijama.com/wet-cupping-hijama-karachi.html

Q: What is wet cupping (hijamat)?
A: Wet cupping, called hijamat in the classical Sunnah tradition, is a therapy in which cups are applied to selected points, a few tiny superficial scratches are made, and the cups are reapplied so a small amount of blood is drawn out. At Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic & Hijama Center in Model Colony, Karachi, it is performed by Dr Misbah Shaheen Cheena using new single-use cups and blades every session.

Q: Is wet cupping in Karachi safe and hygienic?
A: When performed by a trained practitioner using single-use, sterile equipment, wet cupping is generally very well tolerated. We open fresh disposable cups and blades for every patient, never reuse them, and clean the skin before and after. Tell us when you book if you are pregnant, take blood thinners, or have a bleeding disorder, diabetes or anaemia. Wet cupping is not done during pregnancy, and with blood thinners or a bleeding disorder we will usually advise against it or ask you to check with your doctor first.

Q: Which days are recommended for Sunnah hijama?
A: In the Sunnah, hijama is especially recommended on the 17th, 19th and 21st of the Islamic month. We can help you arrange your appointment on an upcoming Sunnah day when you book on WhatsApp.


### Dry Cupping in Karachi — Model Colony | Shaheen Shafi
Source: https://karachihijama.com/dry-cupping-karachi.html

Q: What is dry cupping?
A: Dry cupping is a form of cupping therapy in which cups create gentle suction on the skin with no incisions and no blood drawn. Cups may be left in place for a few minutes or moved along oiled skin (massage cupping). It is gentler than wet cupping and leaves lighter marks. At Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic & Hijama Center in Model Colony, Karachi, it is performed by Dr Misbah Shaheen Cheena.

Q: What is the difference between dry cupping and wet cupping (hijama)?
A: In dry cupping, cups create suction only — no scratches are made and no blood is drawn. In wet cupping (the classical Sunnah hijama), the practitioner also makes a few tiny superficial scratches so a small amount of blood is drawn into the cup. Both are offered as traditional, complementary care; which suits you depends on your comfort and your reason for coming.

Q: Does dry cupping leave marks?
A: Dry cupping can leave round, temporary marks where the cups were placed, usually lighter than with wet cupping. These typically fade over several days. They are not bruises in the painful sense and are a normal, expected effect of the suction.

### Unani Treatment in Karachi — Hakeem in Model Colony
Source: https://karachihijama.com/unani-treatment-karachi.html

Q: What is Unani (Tibb) treatment?
A: Unani, also called Tibb, is a classical system of traditional medicine that treats the whole person based on their temperament (mizaj) and balance. A Unani physician (hakeem) assesses you through consultation, then recommends traditional herbal remedies along with guidance on diet and daily routine. At Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic & Hijama Center in Model Colony, Karachi, Unani treatment is provided by Dr Misbah Shaheen Cheena.

Q: Is Unani herbal medicine a replacement for my doctor?
A: No. Unani is offered as traditional, complementary care that many people value alongside modern medicine — not as a replacement for it. If you have a diagnosed condition or take prescription medicines, please continue with your doctor and tell us about your medicines so your care is coordinated safely.

Q: Can I have Unani treatment and hijama together?
A: Yes. Many patients combine classical Unani herbal care with Sunnah hijama (cupping) as complementary, traditional support. Dr Misbah can advise on a plan that suits you when you book.


### Best Hakeem in Karachi | Unani Doctor, Model Colony Clinic
Source: https://karachihijama.com/best-hakeem-unani-doctor-karachi.html

Q: How do I find the best hakeem in Karachi?
A: Judge a hakeem on things you can actually verify rather than on advertising. Ask whether the practitioner is registered and whether the certificates can be seen at the clinic, look at how clean the premises are and whether single-use equipment is opened in front of you, notice whether you are given unhurried time to explain your problem, and pay attention to how the practitioner speaks about your existing medical treatment. A good hakeem will ask what medicines you already take, will not tell you to stop them, will not promise a cure, and will refer you to a conventional doctor when that is the right thing to do.

Q: What registration should a Unani doctor in Pakistan have?
A: Traditional practice in Pakistan is regulated, so ask to see the paperwork before you begin treatment. Dr Misbah Shaheen Cheena is registered with the National Council for Homeopathy, the National Council for Tibb (Unani) and the Sindh Healthcare Commission, and the certificates are on display at the clinic in Model Colony. Any practitioner who becomes uncomfortable when you ask this simple question is telling you something useful.

Q: What happens in a first Unani consultation?
A: The first visit is mostly conversation. Dr Misbah asks about your complaint and how long it has been going on, your appetite, digestion, sleep, energy and daily routine, and every medicine or supplement you take, then makes a traditional assessment of your temperament, or mizaj, which in the classical method includes feeling the pulse, or nabz, and observing general signs. From that, Dr Misbah suggests a personalised herbal formulation along with practical guidance on diet and lifestyle, and explains what to expect and when to come back.

Q: Can a hakeem replace my regular doctor?
A: No, and you should be cautious of anyone who suggests otherwise. Unani is offered here as traditional, complementary care that sits alongside modern medicine rather than replacing it. If you have a diagnosed condition, please continue with your doctor, keep taking your prescribed medicines, and attend your hospital appointments. Tell us what you are taking so that your care stays coordinated and safe.

Q: Is Unani herbal medicine safe to take with prescription medicines?
A: Herbal preparations are still active substances, so they must be discussed openly rather than taken quietly on the side. Bring your prescriptions or a photograph of them to your appointment, and tell Dr Misbah about any long-term condition, pregnancy or planned surgery. If there is any doubt about combining a remedy with your treatment, the safe course is to check with your treating doctor first, and we would rather you did that than take a risk.

Q: Can I have hijama and Unani treatment on the same visit?
A: Often yes. Herbal care and Sunnah cupping have been used side by side for centuries, and many patients at the clinic combine a Unani consultation with wet or dry cupping. Whether both are suitable on the same day depends on your health and how you are feeling, so mention your interest when you book and Dr Misbah will suggest a sensible plan.

Q: Is a female practitioner available for women patients?
A: Yes. A qualified female practitioner is available for women patients. Please ask when you book so that the appointment can be arranged for a time when she is present.

### Hijama Side Effects & Who Should Avoid It
Source: https://karachihijama.com/blog/hijama-side-effects-and-who-should-avoid.html

Q: How much blood is removed during a Hijama session?
A: In wet cupping, only a small, controlled amount of blood is drawn from tiny superficial skin scratches into each cup — typically a few millilitres per cup, far less than a standard blood donation. It is not enough to cause weakness in a healthy adult. The exact amount depends on the number of cups and areas treated, and we monitor it carefully throughout your session.

Q: What are the normal side effects of Hijama?
A: The most common and expected effect is a set of small, round marks where the cups sat, which usually fade within several days to two weeks — this is a normal, harmless part of the process, not a bruise from injury. Some people feel mildly tired or a little light-headed for a short while afterwards, which usually passes quickly with rest and water.

Q: Who should avoid or postpone Hijama?
A: We generally ask people to avoid or postpone Hijama if they are pregnant, have a bleeding disorder or are on blood-thinning medication, have severe anaemia, have an active skin infection or open wound at the treatment site, are extremely weak or unwell, or have certain serious conditions their doctor has advised caution about. If any of this applies to you, please tell us honestly when you book — we would rather advise you safely than treat you when it isn't right.

Q: Can Hijama cause an infection?
A: The risk is very low when proper hygiene is followed, which is why we use single-use sterile cups and blades for every single patient, and a clean, controlled environment. Following our simple aftercare advice — keeping the area clean and dry for the first day — further reduces any risk.

Q: Are the cupping marks painful or dangerous?
A: No. The circular marks are a normal, expected part of wet cupping and are not painful once the session ends — most people describe mild tenderness at most, similar to a light pinch. They fade naturally over several days to two weeks and leave no lasting damage.

Q: How do I get a safe Hijama assessment in Karachi?
A: Message us on WhatsApp at +92 322 2905560 and tell us honestly about your health, any medication you take, and any conditions you have. We will assess whether Hijama is suitable for you and, if so, arrange a convenient time at Shaheen Shafi Unani Clinic & Hijama Center in Model Colony, Karachi. We are open 3:00 PM to 10:00 PM every day.


### What Is Hijama (Cupping)? Process, Benefits & Aftercare
Source: https://karachihijama.com/blog/what-is-hijama.html

Q: What is the difference between wet and dry cupping?
A: In dry cupping, cups create gentle suction on the skin with no incisions and no blood drawn. In wet cupping (hijama in the classical sense), the practitioner first applies cups, then makes a few tiny superficial scratches and reapplies the cups so that a small amount of blood is drawn out. Both are offered as traditional, complementary care.

Q: Does hijama hurt?
A: Most people describe it as a strong pulling or tightness where the cups are placed, and a brief light scratch during wet cupping, rather than sharp pain. Everyone's tolerance differs. A calm setting and an unhurried practitioner make it more comfortable. Tell your practitioner if anything feels too intense.

Q: Is hijama safe and hygienic?
A: Yes. Performed by a trained practitioner using single-use, sterile cups and blades, hijama is well tolerated and families in Karachi trust it as a calm, clean experience. We open fresh, single-use disposable equipment for every session — never reused — and clean the skin before and after. When you book, just let us know about your health and any medicines so we plan your session safely.

Q: What should I tell you before booking hijama?
A: So we can plan your session safely and comfortably, just let us know when you book if you are pregnant, have a bleeding disorder, take blood thinners, have diabetes or anaemia, have a skin infection at the site, or feel very weak or dehydrated. This helps us tailor your session and choose the gentlest approach for you.

Q: How should I care for myself after hijama?
A: Keep the treated area clean and covered for the rest of the day, drink water, rest, and avoid very hot showers, heavy exercise, and smoking for the rest of the day. The round marks usually fade over several days. If you notice increasing redness, swelling, discharge or fever, contact a doctor.
